goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator contents swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains category fabricators, breaking the entire test suite (P1)

Migration data import doesn't normalize hosts — raw setting values like 'http://eviltrout.com' won't match record_for_host's comparison against uri.host, silently breaking embeddable hosts after upgrade (P1)
Migration interpolates setting values directly into SQL without escaping, crashing on values with apostrophes (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from the `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts` (split by newlines). If any stored host line contains an apostrophe (or other SQL-significant characters), the SQL becomes invalid and the migration can fail; it also bypasses proper escaping/quoting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: save_host crashes with 500 instead of validation error when params missing or host is blank (NoMethodError on nil host) (P2)
Host with port stored (validation allows example.com:8080) can never match referer since record_for_host compares against uri.host without port, silently failing (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the host format validation explicitly allows an optional port (`...(:[0-9]{1,5})?...`). The `before_validation` callback strips scheme and path but does not strip a `:port`, so an entry like `http://example.com:8080` will be stored as `example.com:8080`. However, `record_for_host` parses the referer via `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host` (hostname only, no port) and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That will compare `example.com` against stored `example.com:8080` and fail, causing `host_allowed?` to reject valid referers when the allowed host was stored with a port.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side destroyRecord() has no .catch(popupAjaxError), so delete failures are swallowed with no user feedback (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` but does not attach a `.catch(popupAjaxError)` (or any rejection handler). If the DELETE request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and the user gets no feedback, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? no longer gated on embeddable_hosts.present?, changing behavior for sites that delete all hosts (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic.rb`, `expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing the “embedding enabled / hosts configured” gate entirely. Since the `embeddable_hosts` setting was removed and hosts now live in the `EmbeddableHost` table, this means that even if an admin deletes all allowed hosts (effectively disabling embedding going forward), existing embedded topics (`has_topic_embed? == true`) will still be treated as expandable when `embed_truncate` is on—behavior that previously would have been disabled when no hosts were configured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` adds an uncached DB query to the hot embed path in embed_controller.rb:61 and lib/topic_retriever.rb:16, previously an in-memory settings lookup, materially increasing DB load on every embedded-comments iframe load

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes embed host checks from an in-memory SiteSetting string scan (`SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?`) to a database-backed lookup (`EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`). `host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (a DB query) each time it is invoked. This method is now used on the embed request path in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, and the diff shows no caching layer around these calls. That is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the change, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `where("lower(host) = ?")` on unindexed `host` column in app/models/embeddable_host.rb:18 causes a full table scan per embed request, and lower(host) can't use a btree index on host

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` which queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) and the migration creating `embeddable_hosts` does not add any index on `host` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). So this lookup will be a full table scan and using `lower(host)` would not use a plain btree index on `host` anyway. This is a concrete performance/scalability concern introduced by the diff, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` in admin/embedding_controller.rb:17 loads and serializes all hosts with no pagination/limit on every admin page load

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding` building an OpenStruct with `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` and `show`/`update` always `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`, so the admin embedding page will load and serialize *all* `EmbeddableHost` rows on each page load. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/scalability concern (no pagination/limit), but not a clear correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL string interpolation in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — `host` values interpolated directly into INSERT statement allow injection or breakage from quote/s payloads in saved embeddable_hosts setting

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` inside a loop over `val.split("\n")` (the old `site_settings` value). Because `h` is interpolated directly into a quoted SQL string with no escaping/parameterization, a host containing a single quote (or other SQL) would break the migration and could be used for SQL injection in the migration context. This is verifiable from the diff at the INSERT line.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbeddingSerializer#id` serializes an OpenStruct wrapping an AR relation; `has_many :embeddable_hosts` on an OpenStruct is fragile and relies on the relation materializing once

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding` building `@embedding` as an `OpenStruct` with `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` (an AR::Relation), and `EmbeddingSerializer` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, ... embed: :ids`. This will work, but because the association is a lazy relation on a non-AR object, the serializer may enumerate it multiple times (e.g., once for IDs and again for sideloading), potentially causing repeated queries and making behavior/perf depend on how/when the relation is materialized. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/performance concern, not a guaranteed correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a no-op that renders the serializer without persisting anything, returning 200 success while no update occurs

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action does not apply any params or persist anything; it simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` where `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`. The route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` exists, and the client controller action `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, so a PUT will return a successful serialized response while performing no update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration inserts raw host strings verbatim into embeddable_hosts.host, bypassing the before_validation scheme/path stripping, so previously-configured URL-form hosts silently lose embed permission after upgrade
Migration interpolates the site-setting value directly into SQL ('#{h}'), which can break/skip the migration for values containing quotes; should use bind parameters or EmbeddableHost.create!

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` comes from the stored `site_settings` value split by newlines, any host entry containing a single quote (or other SQL-special characters) will produce invalid SQL and can cause the migration to fail or insert incorrect data. This is a correctness/robustness defect introduced by the diff; using bind parameters or creating records via the model would avoid it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing-record handling in update/destroy returns 500 instead of 404: EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first can return nil, causing NoMethodError in save_host or host.destroy
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` may return nil in update/destroy, leading to `NoMethodError` when calling `save_host` or `destroy`, and notes the lack of proper 404 handling. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: REST adapter basePath change (type.replace('_', '-')) silently re-routes request paths for other underscored ADMIN_MODELS, not just embeddable-host

adjudication.rationale: In `rest.js.es6`, `basePath(store, type)` now checks `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-')) !== -1`. This does not “silently re-route request paths for other underscored ADMIN_MODELS” beyond those already explicitly listed in `ADMIN_MODELS` (`plugin`, `site-customization`, `embeddable-host`). The replacement only affects whether a given `type` string matches one of these known admin model names; it does not expand the set of admin-routed models. At most, it makes underscored inputs like `embeddable_host` or `site_customization` match their dashed entries, which appears intentional given the addition of `embeddable-host`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingSerializer#id returns string 'default' for a non-persisted resource, creating identity-map contract mismatch between PUT /admin/customize/embedding and the Ember store

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally models embedding as a singleton resource: `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding` sets `id: 'default'`, and the Ember adapter `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6` hardcodes `pathFor()` to `"/admin/customize/embedding"` (no `/:id`). The route uses `this.store.find('embedding')` (no id), consistent with a singleton endpoint returning an object with an id. Nothing in the diff shows an identity-map/PUT mismatch (e.g., PUT including an id while GET does not, or differing ids across responses). The presence of a string id `'default'` alone is not a verifiable defect from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost before_validation raises NoMethodError on nil host instead of returning a validation error; controller also 500s on missing params[:embeddable_host] wrapper key instead of render_json_error

P1: embeddable_hosts_controller.rb destroy/update missing nil check on record lookup — EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first can return nil, causing NoMethodError/500; destroy should 404 or return idempotent success_json

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls methods on `host` (`save_host(host)` assigns `host.host = ...`; `destroy` calls `host.destroy`). If no record exists for the given id, `host` will be `nil`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500 response. The diff shows no nil handling (e.g., `find_by!`/404 or idempotent success), so the finding is a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: embeddable-host.js.es6 delete action has unhandled promise rejection — destroyRecord().then(...) lacks .catch(popupAjaxError), so failed deletes give no user feedback and rows silently remain

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: admin-embedding.js.es6 saveChanges is fire-and-forget — this.get('embedding').update({}) discards the promise with no error handling or success feedback; additionally the server-side update action in embedding_controller.rb is a no-op that just re-renders, so 'save' persists nothing

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: migration create_embeddable_hosts crashes if embed_category setting row is absent — execute(...)[0]['id'] raises NoMethodError on nil, blocking db:migrate for upgrades; should use safe navigation/rescue

The later fallback `if category_id == 0` is unreachable in that case because the exception occurs first. adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that just re-renders without persisting, and the client calls it with an empty payload — dead PUT route/button that misleads maintainers; implement real update or remove

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostSerializer's id, host, and category_id methods are exact copies of default behavior — dead code; same in embedding_serializer.rb

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost model's before_validation calls self.host.sub! which crashes with NoMethodError on nil host; should guard with host.present?
Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host doesn't guard params[:embeddable_host][:host] being absent, producing a 500 instead of a validation error

If the request omits `embeddable_host` or its `host` key, this will raise (e.g., `NoMethodError` on `nil[:host]`) and produce a 500 rather than a handled validation/JSON error. The diff shows no guarding (no `dig`, no presence check, no strong params) around these accesses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic.rb:869 expandable_first_post? no longer checks whether embedding hosts are configured (removed embeddable_hosts.present? without replacement like EmbeddableHost.exists?), silently severing flag/host coupling

adjudication.rationale: In Topic#expandable_first_post? the guard `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` was removed (topic.rb change) and there is no replacement check against the new EmbeddableHost-based configuration (e.g., `EmbeddableHost.exists?`). As a result, the method now depends only on `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, which severs the previous “embedding enabled/hosts configured” coupling. This is a real behavior change, but it’s not provably a defect from the diff alone (it may be intentional to allow expandability for already-embedded topics even if no hosts are configured).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable-host.js.es6:36 manually patches host.category via global Discourse.Category.findById instead of using the store's embedded category_id hydration, duplicating logic and risking stale data

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` the `save()` action explicitly does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` after `host.save(props)`. The server response for save uses `EmbeddableHostSerializer` which only returns `category_id` (no embedded `category` object / sideloaded categories), so Ember-store hydration won’t necessarily refresh `host.category` from the save response. Manually patching via the global `Discourse.Category` is extra coupling/duplication and can desync from store-managed relationships/caching, but it’s not a clearly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone (it may be intentional to update the UI immediately).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host ignores ports/schemes asymmetrically: lookup normalizes via URI(host).host but validation permits port suffixes, so port-specific embed rules silently can't work

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, `before_validation` strips scheme and path but does **not** strip the port (`self.host` can remain like `example.com:3000`), and the regex validation explicitly allows an optional `(:[0-9]{1,5})`. However `record_for_host(host)` parses the incoming URL with `URI(host)` and uses `uri.host` (which excludes the port) to query `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That means a saved record containing a port (e.g. `example.com:3000`) will never match requests for `http://example.com:3000/...`, so port-specific allowlisting silently cannot work and may unexpectedly block embeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Migration interpolates unescaped host values into raw SQL, allowing syntax errors or SQL injection from admin-configured embeddable_hosts setting

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds a raw SQL string with unescaped host values from the old site setting: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` comes from `site_settings.value` (`embeddable_hosts`) and is interpolated directly into a quoted SQL literal, a value containing `'` (or other SQL) can break the statement (syntax error) and could potentially be used for SQL injection during migration execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Migration is not reversible — raw execute calls in a change method permanently delete site settings with no reversible down or backup

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses a `change` method with multiple raw `execute` calls (SELECT/INSERT/DELETE), including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Rails cannot automatically reverse `execute` in `change`, so rolling back will raise an irreversible migration error and the deleted `site_settings` values cannot be restored without a custom `down`/`reversible` block. This makes the migration non-reversible and can cause permanent data loss on rollback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: create_table with force: true silently drops an existing table and all its data on re-run or restored environments

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. While migrations normally run once, this is a real, diff-grounded risk during re-run/redo or in restored/partially-migrated environments and can cause silent data loss, so the reviewer concern is valid even if it may not manifest in the typical one-time migration path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Backfill crashes with NoMethodError when the uncategorized_category_id site setting row is absent, and embed_category lookup silently mis-backfills if the category was renamed

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` can raise when expected `site_settings` rows are missing: it does `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i` without checking that the query returned any rows, so `[0]` can be `nil` leading to `NoMethodError`. It also derives `category_id` by joining `site_settings.value` to `categories.name` for `embed_category` (`INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name`), so if the category was renamed after the setting was stored, the join returns no rows, `category_id` becomes 0, and it silently falls back to uncategorized, mis-backfilling hosts into the wrong category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: EmbeddableHostsController#destroy and #update crash with a 500 instead of a 404 when the record is missing due to no nil check

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` but there is no handling for a missing record. In `update`, `save_host(host)` will call `host.host = ...` and crash with `NoMethodError` if `host` is `nil`. In `destroy`, `host.destroy` will likewise crash when `host` is `nil`. This would result in a 500 instead of a 404 for nonexistent IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Data-loss guard removed in Topic#expandable_first_post? — embeddable_hosts.present? check dropped, changing truncation behavior for sites with embed_truncate on but no hosts configured

adjudication.rationale: The diff does drop `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` from `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (topic.rb), so the method now depends only on `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. However, `embeddable_hosts` as a site setting is removed in this PR (site_settings.yml, server.en.yml, SiteSetting method deleted) and replaced by the `EmbeddableHost` model/table, so calling the old guard is no longer possible. The finding’s claimed impact (changed truncation behavior when `embed_truncate` is on but no hosts exist) is plausible for existing embedded topics if all `EmbeddableHost` records are removed, but it’s not clearly a defect nor “data-loss” from what’s shown; it’s a behavioral/UX policy question about whether to also gate on `EmbeddableHost.any?`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TopicEmbed.import silently loses category when host is not registered, falling back to the default category with no error

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the category is now derived from the embeddable host record: `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and `category: eh.try(:category_id)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If `record_for_host` returns `nil` (e.g., host not registered / not found), `PostCreator` receives `category: nil`, which can result in the topic being created in a default/uncategorized category with no explicit error at this call site. The diff does not add any guard/raise here for missing `eh`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Removed site settings not registered as deleted, leaving orphaned settings referencing removed code paths if the migration's delete fails or is skipped

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings from `config/site_settings.yml`, but it also adds a migration (`20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`) that explicitly deletes those rows from `site_settings` at the end (`DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`). The finding’s claim about “not registered as deleted” and “orphaned settings … if the migration’s delete fails or is skipped” is speculative and refers to behavior/mechanisms not shown in the diff; nothing in the diff demonstrates a required “deleted settings registry” or a concrete resulting defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Fabricator files are swapped — spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator and vice versa, leaving :category (and variants) undefined and breaking every spec that fabricates a category

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: the before_validation callback calls `self.host.sub!` and will raise `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil, leading to an exception instead of a validation error. This matches the golden comment’s core issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TopicEmbed.import falls back to no category when EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url) returns nil, diverging from prior embed_category behavior; combined with skip_validations: true, imported topics are silently mis-filed

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the category is now derived from `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passed as `category: eh.try(:category_id)` (so `nil` if no matching host record). The diff does not show a hard guarantee that `TopicEmbed.import` is *only* called after a successful `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` check, so a defensive fallback (e.g., uncategorized) or an explicit failure might be warranted. However, the diff also updates the main gatekeepers (`TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`) to use `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, which likely prevents the nil case in normal flows, so the “silently mis-filed” claim is not verifiably a concrete defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Admin endpoint specs only assert controller subclassing — no tests cover create/update/destroy authorization, validation failures, ensure_staff filter, param handling, or category_id blanking

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial admin endpoints with state-changing behavior and access control (e.g., Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update/destroy and save_host param handling/category_id defaulting; Admin::EmbeddingController#show/update with ensure_staff + fetch_embedding). However, the newly added specs (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) only assert the controllers subclass Admin::AdminController and do not exercise authorization filters, failure paths (invalid host/category), parameter handling, or destroy behavior. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Regex permits host:port entries, but record_for_host compares only uri.host without port, so a stored host like eviltrout.com:8080 can never match a referer with port

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the `host` validation regex allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and the `before_validation` callback strips protocol and path but does not remove any `:port`. However, `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and compares only `uri.host` (no port) against `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. Therefore a stored value like `eviltrout.com:8080` will never match a referer like `http://eviltrout.com:8080/...` (parsed host becomes `eviltrout.com`), making such entries unusable.
